technical_and_design_decisions: Build the increment on the existing Spring XD / Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d) codebase using Spring Boot, Spring Batch (composed job runner), Spring Shell, and Spring Cloud Stream.

U1: Aggregated progress is computed server-side by rolling up child job/step execution progress from the job repository into a single percentage for the composed job, exposed through a REST endpoint and rendered as a progress bar in the admin UI and shell.
U2: Composed job restart is implemented on top of Spring Batch JobOperator restart semantics, persisting the last completed child job/step so a re-launch resumes from the failed or next child job.

U3: Kafka 0.9 work is a time-boxed spike targeting the new Kafka consumer API; a prototype of the spring-cloud-stream Kafka binder changes is produced, but the primary deliverable is a findings/recommendations document.
U4: Lattice work is a time-boxed spike; bootstrap uses scripted provisioning (Vagrant/shell) for bare metal, with a throwaway demo deployment of s-c-d and a findings document as deliverables.
U5: The stream definition parser and property resolution are extended so dot-delimited paths can address nested properties of Tuple and JSON typed module options, with binding validation.
U6: Shell tab completion is implemented via Spring Shell completion/value-provider hooks, sourcing module metadata and option descriptors from the module registry.
U7: Mesos support is implemented as a new deployer SPI implementation that submits modules to Marathon via its REST API, including health checks and scaling attributes.

U8: The redis @Rule test fixture is extracted into a standalone test-support repository with its own Maven/Gradle build and publication to the Spring artifact repository; consuming projects are switched to the published artifact.
assumptions: A single experienced developer (the estimator) performs all work; all figures are effort in work-hours, not elapsed calendar time.
The existing s-c-d / Spring XD codebase, CI infrastructure, source repositories, and a Java 17 toolchain (per spec) are available and functional.
U3 and U4 are investigation/exploration spikes; their deliverables are findings documents and non-production prototypes, so no production hardening is estimated for them.
Test environments (Kafka 0.9 brokers, a small Mesos/Marathon cluster, Lattice cells) can be provisioned by the developer; provisioning effort is included in the relevant activities.
Estimates include unit testing, integration testing, developer/reference documentation, and self-review; no separate QA team or formal test phase is assumed.
The admin UI and shell already exist; only incremental changes are needed (no new UI framework).
Community/peer code review feedback is limited; a fixed cross-story review and rework allowance is included.
No clarifications are required; ambiguous scope items are resolved by the reasonable interpretations stated in the design decisions.
